overview: DAY-NRLM (Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission) is a centrally sponsored scheme launched by the Ministry of Rural Development to reduce rural poverty by promoting diversified and gainful self-employment and skilled wage employment opportunities. It focuses on organizing rural poor women into Self Help Groups (SHGs) and federations, building their capacities, and enabling access to financial and livelihood resources. The scheme aims to achieve universal social mobilization, financial inclusion, and sustainable livelihoods for rural households living below the poverty line.
geographic_scope: Pan-India (rural areas across all states and union territories)
objectives: Organize rural poor women into Self Help Groups (SHGs) and their federations
Build capacities of the poor for livelihood diversification and skill development
Ensure financial inclusion through access to credit, savings, and insurance
Support creation of sustainable livelihoods through farm and non-farm activities
Promote social inclusion and empowerment of marginalized groups
Strengthen institutional platforms of the poor at village, block, and district levels
Facilitate convergence with other government programs for holistic development
Enable access to rights, entitlements, and public services
eligibility: Rural households living below the poverty line (BPL), with special focus on women, SC/ST, persons with disabilities, and vulnerable groups. Eligibility is determined through participatory identification of poor (PIP) at the village level, validated by Gram Sabha. All rural poor are eligible for mobilization into SHGs, with priority given to the poorest and most marginalized.
benefits: Financial inclusion through bank linkage and access to revolving fund and community investment fund; capacity building and skill training; livelihood support for farm and non-farm activities; market linkages and value chain development; social inclusion and empowerment; convergence with other government schemes; access to insurance and risk mitigation instruments; support for rural enterprises and producer groups.
financial_support: Financial support is provided through Revolving Fund (RF) and Community Investment Fund (CIF) to SHGs and their federations. RF is a one-time grant of up to INR 10,000–15,000 per SHG for strengthening group corpus. CIF is provided as a grant to village organisations for on-lending to SHGs for livelihood investments. Interest subvention is also available on loans to SHGs for livelihoods. Support is also provided for skill training, infrastructure, and enterprise development under various sub-components.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 15,000 per Self Help Group (SHG) as Revolving Fund
application_process: 1. Mobilization of rural poor into Self Help Groups (SHGs) through village-level outreach. 2. Formation and training of SHGs on group dynamics, savings, and inter-loaning. 3. Validation of SHGs by Village Organisation and Gram Sabha. 4. Opening of bank account and initiation of regular savings. 5. Application for Revolving Fund (RF) through Village Organisation. 6. Sanction and disbursement of RF by Block Level Federation. 7. Utilization of RF for internal lending and income-generating activities. 8. Eligibility for Community Investment Fund (CIF) based on group performance and grading. 9. Access to CIF for livelihood investments through village organisation.
required_documents: Bank account passbook of the SHG
Member details and BPL status verification
Business plan for livelihood activity (for CIF)
deadlines: Rolling basis — SHG formation and RF/CIF applications are accepted throughout the year based on village-level readiness and validation.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India
caveats: Financial support is contingent on group grading, performance, and adherence to norms
Benefits are accessible only through registered and validated SHGs and village organisations
Funds must be used for approved livelihood and income-generating activities
Misutilization of funds may lead to recovery and exclusion from further support
